results.name: outlier_vs_clean_last_digit_rule
results.description: Among 3-4 example sets, yes rate for unseen targets ending in the majority last digit when exactly one example breaks that digit, minus the same rate when all examples share it; observed > null means people discount a rule-breaking example less (keep the rule more) than the model's uncertain-reliability noise produces, observed < null means one stray undermines the rule more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: outlier_vs_clean_last_digit_rule
# description: Among 3-4 example sets, yes rate for unseen targets ending in the majority last digit when exactly one example breaks that digit, minus the same rate when all examples share it; observed > null means people discount a rule-breaking example less (keep the rule more) than the model's uncertain-reliability noise produces, observed < null means one stray undermines the rule more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    dig = {}
    kind = {}
    for s in sets:
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        if len(v) < 3:
            continue
        ld = [x % 10 for x in v]
        vals, cnt = np.unique(ld, return_counts=True)
        k = int(np.argmax(cnt))
        if cnt[k] == len(v):
            kind[s], dig[s] = 0, int(vals[k])
        elif cnt[k] == len(v) - 1:
            kind[s], dig[s] = 1, int(vals[k])
    ns = df["number_set"]
    kd = ns.map(kind)
    dg = ns.map(dig)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    # vectorised membership test via string matching on padded set
    padded = "," + ns.astype(str) + ","
    tstr = "," + t.astype(str) + ","
    member = np.array([b.find(a) >= 0 for a, b in zip(tstr.values, padded.values)])
    match = (t % 10 == dg) & ~member
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    a = r[match & (kd == 1)]
    b = r[match & (kd == 0)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: participant_set_breadth_heterogeneity
results.description: Mean over sets (>= 15 trials) of the across-participant variance of per-participant yes rates on that set (participants = consecutive blocks starting at trial_index 0); observed > null means people differ in how broadly they generalise from a given set (different chosen concepts) beyond the model's independent-response binomial noise.
results.code:
# name: participant_set_breadth_heterogeneity
# description: Mean over sets (>= 15 trials) of the across-participant variance of per-participant yes rates on that set (participants = consecutive blocks starting at trial_index 0); observed > null means people differ in how broadly they generalise from a given set (different chosen concepts) beyond the model's independent-response binomial noise.
def test_statistic(df):
    pid = np.cumsum(df["trial_index"].values == 0)
    d = pd.DataFrame({"s": df["number_set"].values, "p": pid, "r": df["rating"].astype(float).values})
    cnt = d.groupby("s")["r"].size()
    keep = cnt[cnt >= 15].index
    d = d[d["s"].isin(keep)]
    if len(d) == 0:
        return 0.0
    m = d.groupby(["s", "p"])["r"].mean()
    v = m.groupby(level=0).var(ddof=0)
    return float(v.mean())

results.name: within_run_position_slope
results.description: OLS slope of yes (non-example targets) on log(1 + position within a run of consecutive trials showing the same set); observed > null means people grow more liberal as they keep answering about one set (observed < null more conservative) than the static model produces.
results.code:
# name: within_run_position_slope
# description: OLS slope of yes (non-example targets) on log(1 + position within a run of consecutive trials showing the same set); observed > null means people grow more liberal as they keep answering about one set (observed < null more conservative) than the static model produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    seq = df[["trial_index", "number_set"]].drop_duplicates("trial_index").sort_values("trial_index")
    newrun = (seq["number_set"] != seq["number_set"].shift()).values
    run_id = np.cumsum(newrun)
    pos = pd.Series(seq["trial_index"].values).groupby(run_id).cumcount().values
    pmap = pd.Series(pos, index=seq["trial_index"].values)
    p = np.log1p(df["trial_index"].map(pmap).values.astype(float))
    padded = ("," + df["number_set"].astype(str) + ",").values
    tstr = ("," + df["target"].astype(int).astype(str) + ",").values
    member = np.array([b.find(a) >= 0 for a, b in zip(tstr, padded)])
    x, y = p[~member], df["rating"].astype(float).values[~member]
    if len(x) < 3 or np.var(x) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.cov(x, y, bias=True)[0, 1] / np.var(x))

results.name: single_example_last_digit_match
results.description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets more than 10 from the example that share its last digit minus those that do not; observed > null means people generalise a lone example along its last digit more than the model's "ends in d" rules produce, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: single_example_last_digit_match
# description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets more than 10 from the example that share its last digit minus those that do not; observed > null means people generalise a lone example along its last digit more than the model's "ends in d" rules produce, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    one = ~df["number_set"].astype(str).str.contains(",")
    d = df[one]
    if len(d) == 0:
        return 0.0
    e = d["number_set"].astype(int).values
    t = d["target"].astype(int).values
    r = d["rating"].astype(float).values
    far = np.abs(t - e) > 10
    same = (t % 10) == (e % 10)
    a, b = far & same, far & ~same
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: edge_extension_contrast
results.description: Among non-example targets outside the example range and 1-15 from the nearest example, yes rate when the target lies near the 1-100 boundary (<= 8 or >= 93) minus elsewhere; observed > null means people extend to the ends of the number line more than the model's bounded intervals produce, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: edge_extension_contrast
# description: Among non-example targets outside the example range and 1-15 from the nearest example, yes rate when the target lies near the 1-100 boundary (<= 8 or >= 93) minus elsewhere; observed > null means people extend to the ends of the number line more than the model's bounded intervals produce, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    arr = np.full((len(sets), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(sets):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        arr[i, :len(v)] = v
    idx = pd.Index(sets).get_indexer(df["number_set"])
    ex = arr[idx]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    outside = (t < lo) | (t > hi)
    sel = outside & (d >= 1) & (d <= 15)
    edge = (t <= 8) | (t >= 93)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    a, b = sel & edge, sel & ~edge
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: item_unanimity_rate
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) items (each answered by several participants) on which all answers agree; observed > null means people agree more (the model's item probabilities are too graded), observed < null means people disagree more than the model's item probabilities produce.

results.name: gcd_rule_member_contrast
results.description: Among sets of 2+ examples whose gcd is >= 3, yes rate for unseen targets divisible by the gcd minus unseen targets not divisible by it; observed > null means people generalise along the shared-multiple rule more sharply than the model, observed < null means the model over-commits to multiples rules.

results.name: magnitude_scaled_generalization
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets 4-12 from the nearest example when that example is > 50 minus when it is <= 50; observed > null means people generalise more broadly around large numbers (log/Weber-like similarity) than the model's linear intervals produce, observed < null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: magnitude_scaled_generalization
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets 4-12 from the nearest example when that example is > 50 minus when it is <= 50; observed > null means people generalise more broadly around large numbers (log/Weber-like similarity) than the model's linear intervals produce, observed < null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].unique()
    arr = np.full((len(sets), 4), np.nan)
    for i, s in enumerate(sets):
        v = [int(x) for x in str(s).split(",")]
        arr[i, :len(v)] = v
    idx = pd.Index(sets).get_indexer(df["number_set"])
    ex = arr[idx]
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values[:, None]
    d = np.abs(ex - t)
    d = np.where(np.isnan(d), np.inf, d)
    j = np.argmin(d, axis=1)
    dmin = d[np.arange(len(d)), j]
    near = ex[np.arange(len(d)), j]
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    sel = (dmin >= 4) & (dmin <= 12)
    hi, lo = sel & (near > 50), sel & (near <= 50)
    if hi.sum() == 0 or lo.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[hi].mean() - r[lo].mean())
